A great experience but ask for help when ordering.
Jul 2024 • Friends
Two of us came back to the Barbecue Garden with friends we are traveling with, 10 years after our previous visit. The food was lovely but I would like to caution anyone going for first time about choosing from the menu. It isn’t entirely clear from pictures/descriptions on menu, what meat comes as skewers and what as a plate of marinated meat. So do ask for specific clarification. We over ordered! We also were keen to do our own cooking but staff seemed to come and turn meat immediately after we had, and did not seem to understand that we were happy to cook ourselves. Also, probably should have more than one set of tongs, in this day and age, to prevent cross contamination between seafood, beef and chicken. Surprisingly, in this location, and with a lot of tourists, staff were not strong with English but they were friendly and when we needed to cancel some of the order, were accommodating. Do order a Mocktail for the sheer experience. They came in huge glasses and were superb! (I’m presuming the cocktails do also.)
Overall, an enjoyable meal but some work on the menu or explanation of how to order, by the staff, would be a suggestion to management.

A great choice for the atmosphere
Oct 2023 • Couples
We were walking past the BBQ garden and it looked like a good place for a late lunch. They had a wide choice, the service was good and efficient and the food was very pleasant. Because of this experience we decided to go back for dinner the following night. Dining outside in the garden with coloured lanterns created a very nice atmosphere. You can have the restaurant cook your food or you can do it yourself on a BBQ made up of hot coals in the centre of the table.
The menu had western type food like steak and having been away from home for some time we both opted for different steak dishes. Mistake. Both dishes were tough.
BBQ Gardens is perhaps a great place to have a local dish and drinks, but give the western type foods a miss. It very definitely is a great place for the atmosphere.

Interactive and fun
Dec 2018 • Friends
I’m not one for the choose your own adventure books, particularly those that may involve too much physical exertion. Part of the charm of this city is the contrast it presents in everyday life. The cars and scooters, open approach to what seems to be indicative traffic rules and signage still enables visitors and residents to meander their way down the street, drinking coffee, sipping craft beer and in this hidden garden barbecue up a feast and get creative.
The venue, although in an outdoor courtyard protected by what looks to be a circus tent sized tarp, is clean and the servers are polite and attentive. The menu selection is of a good variety with vegetarian options available. You cant go past their standard beef barbecue selection. Take your time and enjoy a long lunch, you can’t rush the cooking process (it’s not a Weber Q) so best to go with someone that is up for a drink and a chat while you enjoy the smokey smell of Asian barbecue!!

Ideal destination for the meat lover that is in you
Jan 2015 • Family
I have a punchline about Barbecue Garden: it is a rip off! you have to cook your own food! 

Of course I am kidding, but that's the idea in case you are not familiar with this concept that is quite popular in Asian culture. You order raw meat and seafood and you cook it at your leisure on the table, where a small gas powered grill the size of a dish is located. 

I actually enjoy this place, especially if someone else looks after the cooking.

On Sunday 11 January I visited the new location, just a few blocks from the old one on 134 - 136 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street. Barbecue garden is usually packed on evenings, but the new location was half empty. I would recommend the new location, it is cleaner, more space among tables, and the menu and prices are the same. Both locations are open air, but in the new one there is a huge movable ceiling that can protect the place from rain (in the old one they have fixed tents if I recall correctly). 

The menu is quite extensive, you will find any kind of meat and also a good selection of seafood. You can order one of their combos, or you can just make your meal. I was with other two people and we had a big dish with 5 Thai chicken skewers, a lot of beef with cheese, mini tenderloins, a couple of pieces of Australian lamb, some appetizers. The total bill after tax was 30usd. I would say that you can have a good meal for 10-15usd per person, included a beer or bottle of water. Not a bad deal, considered that everything is fresh. And you cannot complain about the cooking...

The service is usually quick and essential. In my last visit I got what I ordered in matters of minutes (in my past visits in the other location even when it was packed I never had any problem about the service). By the way, if you are really allergic to the idea of cooking your meal, a waitress can always be willing to lend you a hand. 

No surprises that the place is popular both with visitors and locals. And barbecue is a Vietnamese tradition, Barbecue Garden just makes it cleaner and more palatable for Westerner visitors. Barbecue Garden is really the Ikea of restaurants... 

Final tip about the new location: if the place is half empty, they will try to squeeze you in the tables closer to the entrance (and the main road). If you need a quiet place, insist on being accommodated in a place near the back.

Rantings from a foreigner
Sep 2014 • Couples
Vietnam… experts in guerrilla warfare, ambushing patrols & taking POW’s, all while disappearing quietly into the night but if the Barbecue Garden Restaurant in HCMC wants to BBQ with the best, they should take it more seriously as if the Chinese were burning villages, so is BBQ a serious business. Most people agree that it’s pretty good here but there is room for improvement, most of my issues might just seem like your whiny First World problems. 

Walking in & seeing fairy lights draped over a huge old tree lighting up the garden, there is a warm ambience in this open al-fresco restaurant setup. The food is good, the smell of cooking meat from every table gets the mouth salivating & eating hot meat straight off a grill is hard not to enjoy. On the other hand, the meat platters are really small here, the pork ribs were very scrawny & the relative cost is high for a Vietnamese meal. Keep in mind you are also supposed to do all the cooking yourself.

At first I assumed this was a Korean BBQ or Japanese style yakiniku restaurant but unlike them they use a gas flame here. The cooking grill was made out of a thin aluminium & isn’t the best for BBQ, I would describe it more accurately as frying meat. I watched as staff applied oil onto the already hot grate which instantly smoked our table up like tear gas in our faces, it stung our eyes making us squint & laugh. They should consider using oil with a high smoke point like extra light olive oil or teach staff to only apply oil on a warn grill. You see, because the meat pieces are so thin & small you have to eat them immediately or they go cold quickly. We preferred to do it ourselves & cook slowly while we talked & drank beer but we found staff constantly rushing over & putting our meat onto the grill all at once. Having to tell them to stop so many times felt like sexual harassment in a Saudi prison. Each time we called for another meat platter, staff would bring it over & put it straight onto the grill then look dumbfounded when we told them to stop. Maybe they should just ask first. 

The bathrooms are just out the back past the motorbikes. They were small & looked like they were banged together cheaply. I couldn’t help but also notice cooks & parking attendants loitering around the toilet entrance while smoking. One or two people isn’t threatening but seeing five-six guys loitering around the toilets isn’t cool, it feels more like a gang of vultures. it’s no big deal but seeing skinny guys squatting & staring at guests as they walk past, entering in & out of a toilet is never going to win you many friends. Now that I mention it, having the kitchen next to the toilet is probably not good for hygiene either, I’m just sayn….

Fantastic meal and great setting
We chanced upon the Barbecue Garden restaurant while walking to another restaurant, and decided to chance it. Were we glad we did.

It has a great menu selection, and the tables have a central gas operated hotplate - you choose your dishes, the waiter brings them over, gives a quick demonstration of how to cook them, and the rest is up to you - you cook your own. We had a bbq meat selection, with 6 different styles of Vietnamese beef - all were delicious.

Service was great and quick, and the prices were very competitive. It's obviously popular with boith locals and tourists - we arrived at 7.00 PM one evening mid week and it was fast fillin g up. When we left, there was a queue of people, including Westerners waiting to get a seat - obviously word has got around). It was the only restaurant in all Vietnam that I saw tourists lined up to get in, so that in itself is an indicator of how good it is.

I'll be back...again...and again...
